label: Subtraction argument and free recombination against the necessary-being nodes
summary: Owner-directed slice (refs #1784), delivering next tests (a) and (b) of attempt 2a1f8da6: the subtraction argument for metaphysical nihilism and free recombination (Hume's dictum) as its support, assessed against the necessary-being nodes STMT-NECESSARY-CONCRETE-AT (b19ffd92) and STMT-NECESSARY-ROOT-BOX-K (cdf897a8). Analyst formulations on the route's own Profile; Baldwin 1996, Rodriguez-Pereyra 1997/2002, Efird and Stoneham 2005, Lowe 1998/2002/2013, Lewis 1986 and Armstrong 1989 are navigation only, no source claim. The subtraction premises are labelled S1-S3, apart from the modal spine's own A2/A3. Findings. (1) Validity and needed premises. S1 (some accessible world has finitely many concreta), S2 throughout (each concretum existing at an accessible world could fail to exist), S3 throughout (conditional subtraction: a concretum that could fail could fail with no newcomer, at one world), transitivity of the route frame (9a6ce384) and excluded middle give 'possibly no concrete object' (result 6aba0bb4, induction on the finite list). S1, S2, S3 and transitivity are each needed: omission models keep the others and falsify the conclusion (infinite tail; theist model; pair model; three-world chain); a nonvacuity model satisfies all. Excluded middle is not omitted in any model: Lean is consistent with it, so no model can omit it and none is needed. The literal S3 ('the non-existence of x does not necessitate the existence of another concretum') is exactly S2 plus the conditional S3 (law 3). (2) Relation to the nodes. The conclusion contradicts the stage-one and box K nodes at their world with no frame condition (laws 1-2). The stage-one node excludes S2 at its world (checked incompatibility 6b12525b, the node as premise and as its own NECESSARY_11 to NECESSARY_2 bridge), and with excluded middle S2 at w is exactly the stage-one node's denial (law 8); for the box K node S2 at w implies its denial but is not equivalent to it. In the theist model on an S5 frame (God at both worlds, one creature at one world) the box K, S5 and stage-one nodes are jointly satisfiable with S1, S3 throughout, transitivity, free absence for candidates that could be absent and companions; S2 fails, and only at the necessary being. So rejecting the subtraction rival requires rejecting only S2; the model shows joint satisfiability, not that the route accepts the other premises. Used against the de re nodes the argument adds no premise beyond the stage-one node's denial; its S1/S3 machinery (from individual contingency to joint absence) bears on the de dicto thesis that no accessible world lacks every concretum. (3) Recombination. Pairwise free absence among distinct concreta with companions gives S2 at w (result 8404e05b; S2 throughout from the same premises at every accessible world is law 5). It does not give S3: in the pair model it holds with S1, S2 and transitivity while S3 and the conclusion fail; the subtraction argument needs a joint principle between pairwise and full recombination. Full recombination over all candidates (the Tractarian ElementaryExistenceAt) gives the conclusion directly (law 4); the box K node already excludes it (065a9092). Restricted to candidates that could be absent, free absence holds in the theist model together with the nodes; the unrestricted form fails there (strict strength order 91a92523). Certified difference 542c595e: unrestricted free absence is exactly the restricted form plus the possible absence of every companioned concrete candidate, and with companions that difference excludes any concrete candidate existing at every accessible world (law 9). Recombination frees the existence of all candidates only in its unrestricted form, whose extra content is that exclusion. The cases that motivate it (separability of ordinary objects in experience) concern candidates both sides take to be contingent; on them the two forms agree, so they do not discriminate. Its standard Humean support, separability in conception, is the conceivability bridge, not assessed at this node. (4) Replies, related to existing nodes rather than re-registered. The analyst formulation of Lowe's reply (a non-concrete candidate existing at every accessible world and co-existing there with some concretum; co-existence only) excludes the conclusion (law 6), and with S1, transitivity and excluded middle it excludes S2 and S3 holding together (law 7), without choosing which fails. It is compatible with every concretum being contingent (pair model), so this formulation alone gives no necessary concrete individual. Lowe's own 2013 modal argument adds an explanatory-dependence premise (roughly, that contingent beings cannot explain the existence of necessary abstracta; navigation only, not checked against the text, not formalized), which would extend the reply toward a necessary concrete being: an unassessed support option for the de re nodes. The route's reply is to deny S2 at the necessary being; that denial follows from the route's arguments for the nodes (four arguments conclude the box K node; the stage-one node has several, e.g. inert emptiness 58ff8235), whose premises stay open. Substantive-objection standard, applied to both sides. Target: S2 at the candidate necessary being (the stage-one node's denial; it excludes the box K node). Mechanism: possible absence of each concretum, then subtraction to a world with none. Independent justification: (i) recombination adds no warrant at the decisive instance beyond its own Humean source (certified difference above); (ii) conceivability of each being's non-existence with a conceivability-to-possibility bridge (existing #248 laws 9bbd9b83: the bridge with a conceived not-H yields possibly not-H, which conflicts with box H) is that source and the only candidate independent support; it is not assessed at this node. From the subtraction argument and recombination, no substantive objection to the de re nodes beyond S2 itself has been identified; no attacks or alternative_to relation is recorded. The route gains nothing here either: its denial of S2 is only as good as its arguments for the nodes. Rejected: recording 'possibly no concrete object' as an alternative_to or attack on the nodes with evidential weight (fails criterion 3 at the decisive instance pending the conceivability assessment); treating the literal S3 as free of S2 (law 3); claiming pairwise recombination supports S3 (pair model); registering the incompatibility at the box K node instead of the weaker stage-one node (the stage-one node suffices and carries its own bridge; the box K node is connected through laws 1-2 and the theist model). Provisional judgment. The disagreement bottoms out at whether some candidate concrete being exists at every accessible world, that is at S2 for the necessary being (the stage-one node's denial). Neither side's derivation begs the question: subtraction is valid, and the nodes are jointly satisfiable with S1 and S3. Recombination adds no warrant for S2 at the necessary being beyond its Humean source, the conceivability bridge, which is unassessed; relative to the case-based motivation (ordinary contingent objects) it begs the question at that instance. The comparison leaves the nodes' standing where their own arguments put it and establishes nothing. Revision conditions: (a) a defended conceivability-to-possibility bridge that applies to a candidate necessary being would give independent support for S2 there and make the subtraction argument a substantive objection; (b) a recombination principle whose warrant covers distinct existences regardless of modal status on independent grounds (Lewis's patchwork principle or Armstrong's combinatorialism, defended without assuming that every concretum is contingent) would do the same; (c) failure of the route's arguments for the nodes would leave S2 at the necessary being uncontested but still unsupported; (d) an argument that a necessary concrete being is incoherent would make S2 analytic; (e) on the other side, a defended explanatory-dependence extension of Lowe's reply would add support for the de re nodes. Frontier and discovery: truth frontier-diff against origin/main reports no change (532 open premises reaching the root before and after, no support alternative added), as intended for a rival assessment; nothing is closed, restated or stacked above a transcription chain. Duper discovery (scripts/run-discovery.sh, --premise-pool all) on the box K, stage-one, S5 and JointAbsence nodes: before, 4 targets, 0 proved, 4 unresolved; after, the same 4 plus 5 new statements, 1 proved (contingent free absence from unrestricted free absence) and filtered as known (it composes from this batch's strength argument 684f95cd), 0 new discoveries, 8 unresolved. The search did not find the incompatibility or the recombination-to-S2 step on its own.
blocker: S2 at the candidate necessary being is the open crux, not decided by the formal results. Next tests: (1) the conceivability route at this node: instantiate the #248 StrongBridge laws with the route's existence valuation and compare the bridge with the reply that conceiving a being's non-existence shows ignorance of its essence, not possibility (Aquinas ST I q.2 a.1, navigation); (2) formalize an explanatory-dependence extension of Lowe's reply (navigation: Lowe 2013, attribution deferred) and test whether it yields a necessary concrete individual on the route profile; (3) a joint subtraction restricted to contingent concreta concluding 'possibly only necessary concreta exist', and its relation to the inert-emptiness premises of 58ff8235; (4) the analyst Lowe co-existence premise against pure sets.
